reference: An independent second implementation of the declared model, written in Python from a first-principles derivation (mass balance on the line volume; one-dimensional isentropic orifice flow assembled as rho*w from the stagnation relations) and solved by a structurally different route: because dm/dt = f(m) is autonomous and one-dimensional, the trajectory is the quadrature t(m) = integral dm/f(m), which contains no time step at all. Cross-routes: an implicit stiff time march (scipy Radau, rtol 1e-12) and closed forms on the choked branch. Anchored to published compressible-flow data. The tool's JavaScript was read only for input names, units, declared assumptions, the declared 1e-9 kg empty-line floor and the list of reported quantities; nothing was transcribed.
reference_citations: A. H. Shapiro, "The Dynamics and Thermodynamics of Compressible Fluid Flow", vol. 1, Ronald Press, New York, 1953, ch. 4: eq. 4.14 (T_t/T), eq. 4.15 (p_t/p), eq. 4.18-4.19 (the critical pressure ratio r* = (2/(g+1))^(g/(g-1))), eq. 4.21 (mass flux per unit area at the throat).

Ames Research Staff, "Equations, Tables and Charts for Compressible Flow", NACA Report 1135, 1953, Table I, isentropic column at M = 1 for gamma = 1.4: p/p_t = 0.528282, T/T_t = 0.833333, rho/rho_t = 0.633938. Reproduced by the reference to 4.0e-7, 4.0e-7 and 2.3e-7 relative, inside half the last printed digit.

The three-significant-digit engineering form of the choked-orifice law for air, mdot = 0.0404 Cd A p_t / sqrt(T) (ISO 6358; Perry's Chemical Engineers' Handbook 8th ed. eq. 10-25). The reference gives 0.0404149, 3.7e-4 relative from the published three-digit constant.

CoolProp 8.0 (Lemmon et al. air EOS; Setzmann & Wagner methane EOS), used to confirm the reference collapses onto the ideal-gas limit at low pressure and to size the fidelity of the declared closure: Z = 0.8880 for methane at 6 MPa and 288.15 K, so the tool's own ideal-gas assumption is 12.6 % out in density at its default supply pressure.
scipy 1.17 solve_ivp with the Radau IIA implicit collocation method, rtol 1e-12, used as an independent second numerical route to the same equations.
provenance_note: Independent second implementation, external to the page (bench-src/gen_gasline_packing.py); the in-page self-checks are carried through separately and labelled as such. All 456 graded references are recomputed during this run and none reuses a stored or published number: 436 by that external implementation, which shares no code with the page, and 20 by the page's own retained in-page self-checks, labelled reference_kind = "self-check" and counted separately; the published anchors are reported under reference_self_verification and carry no graded case.
independent_validation_note: The reference shares no code with the tool and was derived and written separately, which is what the benchmarked tier asserts. It is still the author's own harness: no third party has reviewed it, so independent_validation stays false and no validation.review record exists.
tolerance: Four bands, each fixed by the physics or by what the page prints, none by any step size. (1) Closed-form identities -- the ideal-gas state closure p = m R T / V and the density the page reports from it -- are exact arithmetic on both sides and are held to 1e-12 relative. (2) Marched quantities (terminal pressure, inventory, inventory change, inlet flow, peak inlet flow, terminal instant) are held to 1e-5 relative: that is two orders inside what the page prints (line pressures to 0.01 bar, about 2.5e-4 relative at its own default) and four orders inside the 12.6 % density error the declared ideal-gas closure itself carries at the default 60 bar supply (CoolProp 8.0 methane, Z = 0.8880). (3) The window-invariance families are held to a 1e-6 relative spread: the terminal answer is a property of the line, the gas and the two boundary flows, and the simulated-time window is not one of them, so the only admissible spread is residual discretisation noise. (4) The line pressure may never exceed max(p0, p_supply); that is a hard consequence of having no reverse flow and no heat input, and carries round-off slack only.
grading: total counts every check carrying an acceptance criterion. 436 of them are external to the page: 360 single-case checks against the independent Python reference over 40 input sets, 20 window-invariance checks over 6 families, and 56 checks over 8 input sets on the page's own Python export, compared both with the browser and with the independent reference. The remaining 20 are the superseded in-page checks, retained with their ids and verdicts and labelled reference_kind = "self-check" because they re-evaluate the tool's own relations inside the tool. Rows marked graded = false report the state of a solved case and carry no criterion.

not_benchmarked: Distributed line dynamics: axial pressure gradient, line friction and wave propagation. The model is a single lumped control volume by declaration.
Thermal behaviour. The control volume is isothermal at the input temperature, so neither the heat of compression while packing nor the cooling while depacking is modelled or checked.

Real-gas compressibility. The reference deliberately solves the same ideal-gas closure the tool declares, so the 12.6 % density error that closure carries for methane at 6 MPa is measured (CoolProp) but not corrected: both sides share it.
Discharge-coefficient physics. Cd is an input to both sides, not a modelled quantity.
The convergence ORDER of the RK4 stepper. The harness measures whether the shipped step is converged and whether the answer is invariant to the window, but does not fit a rate.
notes: Regenerate with: python3 gen_gasline_packing.py --dir <dir holding gasline_packing.html and the three shared scripts at their ?v= anchors> --port 8822 --out gasline_packing.json

The reference verifies itself before it is allowed to grade anything: 21 checks covering the published anchors, two analytic limits derived separately, agreement between three structurally different routes, convergence under node refinement, the exponential approach law at equilibrium and the physical pressure bound over 120 pseudo-random legal input sets. The harness refuses to run if any of them fails.

The window-invariance families are the check the superseded artifact could not make: its acceptance band for the terminal pressure was the pressure one solver step moves, with dt = tEnd/800, so the band grew in proportion to the error source and no step size could ever fail it.
